Bitcoin fell back below $60,000, reversing its Thanksgiving recovery from above $62,000 and trading near $59,250 on November 28.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $5.78 billion in November net outflows, while a $7 billion options expiry and $478 million in crypto liquidations added to market volatility.

Bitcoin’s attempt to recover above $62,000 has failed, exposing the weakness beneath its latest rebound. The world’s largest cryptocurrency surrendered its Thanksgiving gains as institutional withdrawals, derivatives volatility and cautious positioning continued to weigh on demand. The reversal is particularly notable because US equities advanced during the shortened holiday trading session, while Bitcoin price moved in the opposite direction.Â

Although large holders have continued accumulating during the correction, their buying has yet to offset persistent ETF outflows. With BTC trading below $60,000 again, the market is approaching another important technical test.

Bitcoin climbed towards $62,125 on November 27 before reversing sharply and falling to approximately $58,719. The move erased most of its Thanksgiving recovery, leaving BTC near $59,250 on November 28.

The decline followed an extended period of weakness. Bitcoin closed near $81,255 on October 28 and around $59,857 on November 27, representing a monthly decline of approximately 26.3%. Its recovery attempts have repeatedly struggled to attract sustained buying above important resistance levels.

Institutional flows remain a central concern. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $5.78 billion in cumulative net withdrawals during November through November 27. Friday alone brought another $389 million in withdrawals, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for $327.2 million.Â

Derivatives activity added another layer of pressure. Approximately $7 billion in Bitcoin options contracts expired on Deribit on November 27, while liquidations across the broader cryptocurrency market reached approximately $478 million. The expiry coincided with Bitcoin’s reversal from above $62,000, although it should not be treated as the sole cause of the decline.Â  The broader picture suggests that institutional demand has not yet recovered sufficiently to support a sustained price rebound.

Despite the ETF withdrawals, on-chain data reveal a contrasting trend among large Bitcoin holders. On-chain data showed that addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC accumulated approximately 121,117 BTC between September 30 and November 21. Their combined holdings increased by 4.29% to approximately 2.95 million BTC, marking the largest fourth-quarter accumulation in absolute terms since 2020.

The same period saw addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC record approximately $2.1 billion in net realized losses. This suggests that some large holders have been buying while other investors have been exiting positions at substantial losses.

The divergence between whale accumulation and ETF withdrawals highlights two different sources of market demand. Large private holders appear willing to increase exposure at lower prices, while investors using regulated exchange-traded products continue reducing their positions.

For Bitcoin to establish a stronger recovery, whale accumulation will need to coincide with improving spot demand and stabilising institutional flows. Until then, buying from large wallets may provide support without being sufficient to reverse the broader downtrend.

Bitcoin’s price chart shows a deteriorating technical structure. After failing to sustain its recovery above $80,000, BTC formed successive lower highs and broke below several previous support areas. The latest decline has pushed the price towards $59,000, with major moving averages remaining above the current market level.

The immediate recovery hurdle sits around $64,000â$66,000, where the chart identifies a previous consolidation and supply zone. A sustained daily close above this region could improve the short-term structure and bring the $73,000â$75,000 area into focus.

On the downside, $56,000 represents the major support zone highlighted on the chart. Bitcoin’s ability to defend this region will be important for preventing another significant breakdown. A decisive move below it could expose the market to further selling pressure.

Bitcoin’s recovery now depends on whether buyers can absorb continued ETF withdrawals and defend the $56,000 region. Whale accumulation offers a counterweight to institutional selling, but it has not yet produced a sustained reversal. A move above $66,000 would strengthen the recovery case, while a breakdown below $56,000 could deepen the correction.

#5091. Ripple’s XRP Ledger Lending Protocol Eyes Final Activation

The XRP Ledger lending protocol proposed by leading blockchain firm Ripple is making the headlines as it appears to be rapidly moving closer to its final debut.

The latest reports on its progress show that the protocol is just one validator vote away from concluding its mandatory approval process on the network.

Barely a few weeks after Ripple proposed a lending protocol on the XRP Ledger, the lending protocol amendment has already secured 28 of the 35 validator votes required to begin the approval process.

This marks major progress for the development, as the XRPL amendment system requires that a proposal earn more than 80% support from trusted validators for two consecutive weeks before it becomes permanently enabled.

While the approval period is mandated to restart if support falls below that level during the countdown, it appears that the Ripple lending protocol is already set to wrap up this process, as it is just one more vote away from reaching the 29-vote milestone.

This means that the lending vaults may be on track for their activation on December 9 if the lending protocol amendment retains the ongoing support.

With the proposed protocol drawing closer to its final launch, the XRP community has continued to express excitement as the proposal aims to introduce fixed-term, fixed-rate lending directly on the XRP Ledger.

As such, users will be able to deposit assets including the Ripple stablecoin and earn interest from borrowers, providing additional ways to earn money.

It is important to note that the proposal aims to provide exclusive opportunities for both lenders and borrowers while further expanding Ripple’s $837 million stablecoin market.

#5086. How to Claim Bitcoin Hyper as Presale Ends With $33M Raised and Token Trading Begins

Bitcoin has joined a broader rebound in risk assets as US markets reopen for a shortened session after Thanksgiving. Bitcoin has joined a broader rebound in risk assets as US markets reopen for a shortened session after Thanksgiving. The top cryptocurrency has risen about 1.8% so far today and is trading near $61,600, putting it on course to snap seven straight weekly losses if the gain holds through Sunday. Stocks have led the move, with Nasdaq-100 futures up more than 2%, while silver has jumped around 7% and gold has added roughly 2.5%.

The recovery follows a difficult stretch, as Bitcoin still remains down over 20% in November (its largest monthly decline since June), and US spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded monthly outflows of $5.39 billion. The Fear and Greed Index sits at 11, signaling extreme fear, and roughly $7 billion in Bitcoin options expired earlier today with traders positioned defensively. Total crypto market capitalization stands near $2.1 trillion, up 1.09% on the day, with Bitcoin’s own market cap at $1.23 trillion.

While prices stabilize and caution lingers, the BTC Layer 2 project Bitcoin Hyper (HYPER) has closed its presale, which raised $33.3 million since it began in May last year. Participants are now able to claim their HYPER tokens, which can also be traded on the top DEX platforms Uniswap and Raydium. Bitcoin Hyper’s strong raise and timely token generation event highlight sustained interest in infrastructure that can expand Bitcoin’s practical uses, setting the stage for the project’s next development steps.

Bitcoin Hyper (HYPER) is aiming to be the fastest true Bitcoin Layer 2 network. It integrates the Solana Virtual Machine to deliver high throughput and low latency, allowing near-instant Bitcoin transactions at minimal cost while settling security back to Bitcoin’s Layer 1. Users deposit native BTC into a Canonical Bridge, which verifies Bitcoin block headers and transaction proofs before minting equivalent wrapped BTC on the Layer 2.

That wrapped BTC can then move freely for payments, decentralized finance activity, staking, and on-chain applications. Withdrawals reverse the process, returning BTC to the user’s Layer 1 address after state verification.

The HYPER token functions as the network’s native utility asset. It covers gas fees for transfers and smart-contract interactions, supports staking for rewards, and grants access to advanced features and governance participation. Token allocations direct 20% to marketing, 15% to rewards, 30% to development, 25% to the project’s treasury, and 10% to major exchange listings.

Hyper Mainnet is now secured by @hackenclub 🔓 ⚡

Final Report: https://t.co/nSJy3Ys8mY pic.twitter.com/zY1ahvp7dQ

— Bitcoin Hyper (@BTC_Hyper2) November 26, 2026

The Bitcoin Hyper network’s architecture relies on a hybrid design (audited by Hacken), in which the Layer 2 handles execution via the Solana Virtual Machine and a Proof-of-Stake validator set, while Bitcoin’s Proof-of-Work system provides periodic anchoring for state integrity.

The completed HYPER presale, which drew $33.3 million, shows clear demand for these capabilities. With the token generation event now finished, buyers can access their allocations as the project moves forward with its Layer 2 deployment timeline.

The Bitcoin Hyper claiming process begins on the project’s official website. Users should first hard-refresh the page to clear the cache, then connect the same wallet employed during the presale. Two options will be available: a standard claim or a claim-and-stake choice.

Solana purchases will need to be claimed on Solana with the original wallet; Ethereum, BSC, or credit-card purchases can be claimed only on Ethereum. Credit card buyers can locate the registered wallet address on their Wert receipt.

Best Wallet holders can claim directly through the app’s Upcoming Tokens section; mobile users should also get smoother results by opening the site inside the wallet’s built-in browser. The project recommends keeping $10–20 worth of ETH or SOL on hand for gas fees incurred during the claim process.

The team will never request private keys or seed phrases, and claims can be completed only through the official site or through Best Wallet. A full guide to claiming HYPER has been published on X via the official Bitcoin Hyper account.

Full claim instructions on the official Hyper TG 👇https://t.co/iukXzZWfcX pic.twitter.com/6SneDFHPBO

— Bitcoin Hyper (@BTC_Hyper2) November 26, 2026

HYPER is available for trading on Uniswap and Raydium. Staked tokens become claimable starting December 3, and any tokens staked after the presale ends will be claimable exactly seven days later. The project is continuing its progress toward the Layer 2 mainnet launch on December 3, when staked allocations unlock and additional network components go live.

This sequence keeps Bitcoin Hyper on track to broaden Bitcoin’s utility through faster settlement and expanded application support, reinforcing a positive outlook for the token as the leading cryptocurrency’s everyday functionality expands.

Salesforce's crypto exposure comes mainly through venture investments in blockchain infrastructure, compliance and fintech businesses.

TRM Labs reached a reported $2B valuation, while Blockdaemon's secondary estimate fell below its 2022 valuation.

Robinhood is one of the few publicly traded company in the crypto-related portfolio list of Salesforce.

Salesforce reports earnings on December 2, and crypto investors have another reason to look beyond its headline financial results.

Its Salesforce crypto investments offer exposure to blockchain infrastructure, compliance software and stablecoin payments.

But don’t mistake that for a company betting its balance sheet on Bitcoin or altcoins.

The distinction matters heading into earnings. Salesforce’s crypto connections are largely through private businesses and fintech investments, not publicly traded tokens.

Salesforce is still the one measuring $8.8B in Thanksgiving sales, then it reports Dec 2.Options are pricing an ~11.5% move in $CRM. IGV already ripped 6.4% this week to $97.53.If AI already killed the apps, why is the software tape bid? Buying the print or fading it?

Salesforce Ventures has backed blockchain-focused companies including Blockdaemon, TRM Labs, Circulor and Mnemonic.

Their businesses cover institutional staking infrastructure, crypto compliance, supply-chain tracking and Web3 data analytics.

The valuations are worth watching. TRM Labs reached a reported $2 billion valuation in September 2026.

Blockdaemon, meanwhile, had an estimated secondary-market valuation of $741 million to $800 million in November, down from its $3.25 billion valuation in 2022.

That’s a substantial difference, although private-market estimates aren’t equivalent to public share prices.

Salesforce’s crypto exposure also extends into fintech. Its portfolio includes Stripe, which supports stablecoin payments and owns Bridge, alongside Airwallex and Flutterwave, which have stablecoin or blockchain payment connections.

Stripe’s valuation reportedly reached $159 billion in February, with November tender discussions pointing above $200 billion.

Airwallex was valued at $11 billion in June, while Flutterwave reached $3.2 billion.

These are private-company valuations, not confirmed returns for Salesforce.

Robinhood is one of the few publicly traded company in the Salesforce portfolio list, with a market capitalisation of approximately $61.2 billion on November 28.

It’s a visible market reference, not a direct measure of Salesforce’s investment performance.

The bigger question for earnings is whether Salesforce discusses its strategic investments, enterprise blockchain opportunities or stablecoin-related business connections.

Crypto-related links could eventually show up in revenue or profit figures. However, there is no guarantee that Salesforce gained any financial contribution from them.

For now, Salesforce crypto investments provide indirect exposure to the industry’s infrastructure and financial rails. Investors shouldn’t confuse or assume portfolio valuations will drive the December 2 results.

#5082. Cardano’s Next Chapter: Euler Named as Major Upgrade After Dijkstra

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Cardano is already looking beyond its upcoming Dijkstra hard fork, with Euler emerging as the next major upgrade.

In a recent release, Intersect, a member-based organization in the Cardano ecosystem, said it is planning the next Cardano upgrade, Euler, with the first meeting of the Euler Scoping Working Group scheduled for December 1, 2026, at 5 p.m. UTC. Here, participants will contribute to early discussions on the scope of the next Cardano era.

The development signals Cardano's continued commitment to evolving its blockchain infrastructure through a structured upgrade process. While Dijkstra represents the current focus, discussions on Euler will set the tone for what comes next for the network.

The Dijkstra era delivers Cardano's major protocol upgrade in two phases: Phase 1, Dijkstra hard fork (Protocol Version 12), introduces the Dijkstra ledger era and ships Ouroboros Linear Leios as a complete, activated feature. The second phase activates Ouroboros Peras via an intra-era hard fork. Peras is a settlement-speed upgrade that adds a voting overlay to the existing Ouroboros Praos chain selection rule.

As of the latest update by Intersect, Dijkstra ledger features are currently being tested on DijkstraNet, while Linear Leios consensus and throughput are being tested on MusashiNet. Both are converging toward Node 11.3, which is the target hard fork release candidate.

The Dijkstra upgrade requires both constitutional and technical changes in the era of on-chain governance. Discussions and refinements on constitutional guardrails (Update Constitution) or CAP-12 "Dijkstra era parameters" continue on the Constitutional Amendment Portal ahead of Mainnet submission.

Protocol Version 12 has already gone live on Musashi and DijkstraNet, while a hard fork release candidate (11.3) is required for Preview and Preprod hard forks. In its recent post, Intersect sets the Dijkstra hard fork target timeline as December 2026 for the Preview network, including the Update Constitution and hard fork.

On-chain activation of the Update Constitution action on the mainnet is expected in December 2026, while the Dijkstra hard fork is expected in Q1 2027.

#5080. Why XRP Analysts Flag $8.30 Macro Price Target

Home » Ripple (XRP) » Why XRP Analysts Flag $8.30 Macro Price Target

The wild SWIFT replacement claim resurfaces on social media for a good reason: XRP-tied banks are in.

Two recent posts have put long-term XRP price projections back in view. One centers on a multi-year chart pattern with an $8.30 target, while the other argues that full replacement of SWIFT would support valuations above $15,000. XRP is trading near $0.95.

Analyst EGRAG CRYPTO highlighted a weekly chart showing a large symmetrical triangle that XRP broke out of in prior years. The X post stated that the original white triangle’s measured breakout target of $8.30 has not yet been reached and suggested the current price action could represent a macro retest of that breakout before any larger expansion.

#XRP – The $8.30 Number 🎯:This remains one of my most powerful macro charts.The original white symmetrical triangle breakout target has STILL not been reached.What if everything happening right now is simply the macro retest of that breakout before the real expansion?My… pic.twitter.com/F0tdM5mxtl

The chart marks $1.65 as a major reclaim and confirmation level, with $8.30 labeled as the primary macro target. EGRAG noted a personal connection to the number.

Being born in 1983, and said that level is where a large portion of holdings would be sold if reached. The analysis frames the target as a technical outcome rather than an emotional one. XRP remains well below its 2025 high near $3.65, and the pattern’s interpretation is subject to debate among traders.

A separate post by Ripple_Mino claimed that if XRP fully replaces SWIFT, the token could be valued beyond $15,000. The argument rests on XRP’s divisibility: one XRP equals one million drops, so even extreme valuations would still allow practical fractional use.

When XRP replaces Swift, it will be valued beyond $15,000 per token.The original token design allowed for such a valuation as 1 XRP can be divided into 1,000,000 smaller units known as drops.So 1 Drop = 0.000001 XRP(one millionth of an XRP) pic.twitter.com/WcBEPSh0XA

Official and recent developments do not support the premise of XRP’s SWIFT replacement.

SWIFT has launched its own blockchain-based shared ledger for tokenized bank deposits, with more than a dozen major banks participating in trials. SWIFT has not announced any integration of XRP as a settlement asset for that system.

Former SWIFT innovation leadership has publicly rejected claims of XRP integration, and the network continues to emphasize its own infrastructure and tokenized deposits rather than a single external token.

The $8.30 figure is a technical target drawn from a multi-year chart structure, while the $15,000 figure is a hypothetical based on a scenario that SWIFT and major participating banks haven’t endorsed yet.

Neither projection is reflected in current market pricing yet or officially top-confirmed institutional commitments. XRP’s price action continues to trade well below both levels as of late November 2026.

The link between SWIFT as a traditional financial intermediary and XRP’s native chain comes multi-layered, with intersection across liquidity provision and instant settlement environments.

Crypto traders who bet on a decline lost nearly $170 million to liquidations over the past 24 hours as Bitcoin, Solana and XRP rose on Black Friday. Short positions made up 68.3% of the $248.8 million in total liquidations.

CoinGlass data showed on Friday that liquidations hit 72,023 traders over that period, and Binance accounted for 44.9% of the total. The largest single order was a $9.3 million BTCUSDT short on Binance, which CoinGlass recorded at a price of $62,147.

Bitcoin shorts lost $64.9 million over 24 hours, and Bitcoin longs lost $20.9 million, according to CoinGlass. On the CoinGlass heatmap, shorts made up 75.7% of Bitcoin's $85.8 million in liquidations across all trading pairs. Bitcoin was trading at around $61,400 on Friday, up 0.9% over 24 hours.

CoinGlass recorded $139.6 million of the short liquidations in the past 12 hours, against $29.9 million in long liquidations over the same window.

Ethereum shorts lost $38.1 million, the second-largest amount among all assets on CoinGlass. ETH traded at around $1,721 on Friday, up 1% over 24 hours.

According to CoinGlass, Solana gained 3.3% to around $73, and SOL shorts lost $6 million. XRP rose 1.9% to $0.97, and its shorts lost $2 million.

BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes warned about the weekend in an X post on Friday. "If there is no Fed dovish rhetoric pivot before the pre-FOMC blackout begins EOD Fri US time, this weekend could get spicy," Hayes wrote. He added that liquid assets and crypto could get dumped before Monday's open.

Earlier this week, Hayes said that Bitcoin "will retest $55k" and shared a chart with the price at $58,773. On Nov. 21, Bitcoin fell as low as $55,150, its lowest price since September 2024.

At its October meeting, the Fed held its benchmark rate at 3.75%–4% in a 10–2 vote. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack voted for a quarter-point hike.

The Fed's blackout period starts at midnight ET on Nov. 28, and the FOMC will announce its rate decision on Dec. 9. CME FedWatch put the odds of a 25-basis-point hike at 100% on Nov. 12.

#5077. XRP Updates: The Ambitious Projects That Contribute to Its Widespread Adoption

XRP has earned a reputation as one of the fastest and lowest-cost cryptocurrencies for payments, powered by the XRP Ledger. The Ripple company, under which both technologies thrive, has positioned itself as a tool for companies that want to modernize their infrastructure and approach decentralization effortlessly. The platform supports more than 1,000,000 custody wallets, enabling […]

XRP has earned a reputation as one of the fastest and lowest-cost cryptocurrencies for payments, powered by the XRP Ledger. The Ripple company, under which both technologies thrive, has positioned itself as a tool for companies that want to modernize their infrastructure and approach decentralization effortlessly.

The platform supports more than 1,000,000 custody wallets, enabling users to settle in 3 to 5 seconds. Crypto businesses, payment services providers, and FinTechs can leverage Ripple’s payment system, so use cases are numerous and convincing for investors to buy XRP.

The popularity and growing interest have contributed to the project’s expansion, including securing additional licenses, extending its escrow functionality, and exploring the possibility of native XRP staking, according to the latest news. A lot is going on in the Ripple ecosystem, so let’s explore more about these additions.

The ledger is known for its high performance, low cost, and appeal for streamlined development, making it the perfect option for business use. That’s what the latest upgrade is about, the “Permissioned DEX”. According to the project documentation, the upgrade will allow regulated institutions to manage traded venues on-chain or benefit from a controlled version of the XRPL decentralized exchange.

The supposed administrators of the venues can delegate trades by checking who can place and accept them, which supports a members-only marketplace for different organizations. This will be possible in accordance with compliance requirements, including KYC (Know Your Customer) and AML (Anti-Money Laundering) procedures.

The benefits of this update include increased liquidity and a blockchain-based settlement system, enabling companies to better manage counterparty eligibility. Moreover, users can benefit from the ledgers’ security, but access to information will be restricted accordingly.

When it comes to official banks using XRP, the EU isn’t necessarily the leading region; Asia-Pacific is the leading region. However, this will change soon, as Ripple has received an important approval from the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority for its EMI (Electronic Money Institution) license.

The announcement was soon followed by another approval by Luxembourg’s financial regulator, CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier). Both regulations strengthen Ripple’s trust across Europe by demonstrating the company’s willingness to operate in accordance with comprehensive digital asset regulations.

Ripple has expanded its regulatory footprint to over 75 licenses globally, and the platform now supports more than 90% of daily foreign exchange markets. Therefore, it is ready to lead the global industry into the next era of financial innovation by securing both compliant operations and advanced technologies such as blockchain.

Hyperliquid is one of the fastest-growing decentralized exchanges, with its own blockchain and specializing in perpetual futures trading. Its low fees, favorable leverage levels, and a vast array of assets have made the decentralized exchange an innovative tool in the industry, and Ripple eyed its potential for collaboration.

By integrating Hyperliquid into its prime brokerage platform, Ripple offered institutional customers the chance to leverage on-chain derivatives liquidity while accessing numerous asset classes, from crypto to foreign exchange. The efforts mark the start of a new trend that addresses decentralized exchanges supporting all sorts of assets.

Of course, the collaboration increased the value of Hyperliquid’s native token, HYPE, making it more efficient for users to transact on the blockchain. However, XRP also saw a boost in value following the announcement, showcasing the power of industry collaborations.

The native token of XRPL has seen considerable appreciation for its transaction benefits, but its journey has also faced challenges. Ripple’s court case with the SEC left a question mark regarding the company’s commitment to the global business sector, despite Ripple’s victory after five years of proceedings.

The SEC accused Ripple of facilitating the sale of unregistered securities, which sparked endless disputes over what cryptocurrencies truly are and what the SEC’s stance is on crypto technology. XRP also saw lower prices during this period due to reduced interest in a company facing court cases. In the meantime, the SEC’s management also changed with a more crypto-oriented approach.

Besides these issues, Ripple has continued to expand and is thriving, leading us to believe the future will follow a similar path. Considering the growing number of collaborations with other industry companies and the interest in advanced technological tooling, Ripple might become a competitive brand in the future of Web3.

While the price of XRP still hasn’t reached the heights of Bitcoin or Ethereum, it still has the potential to be useful for real-world cases. As one of the largest coins by market capitalization, XRP is slowly but steadily being adopted by brands that want to offer users the option to pay with crypto, especially since it operates at fast speeds and low fees.

Therefore, XRP is a suitable investment for a diversified portfolio, as it’s supported by active real-world integration and a global user base. As experts forecast rising prices and expanded adoption in the future, investing in it can help build a stable, reliable long-term portfolio.

For those who don’t want to buy the actual coin and only benefit from exposure, they can invest in XRP ETFs, as several SEC-approved ETFs are available on the market from Grayscale or 21Shares. Each listing has different fees, but they may change. In addition, more XRP ETFs will launch in the future as new funds are launched.

XRP is one of the most controversial cryptocurrencies due to its court case with the SEC, but this hasn’t fully affected the brand and its efficiency. Following the victory over the SEC, XRP continued to expand its use cases and collaborations to better support future adoption. For example, some of the latest additions to the Ripple ecosystem include new regulations in the EU and a partnership with a decentralized exchange.

#5075. Ripple Scores Major Turkish Custody Deal as Analyst Unveils $16T Payment Master Plan That Could Supercharge XRP to $600

Ripple’s push into traditional finance is gaining another major foothold after the company secured a digital asset custody partnership with Turkish banking giant Yapı Kredi. The latest deal adds to Ripple’s expanding institutional footprint as it targets the multitrillion-dollar payments and treasury markets through acquisitions.

But could this growing financial empire eventually translate into an extraordinary XRP price rally? Crypto pundit Vincent Van Code believes the opportunity could be much bigger than the market currently appreciates, outlining a scenario in which XRP climbs to as high as $600.

According to a recent blog post, Ripple’s latest push into traditional finance has taken it deeper into Türkiye’s banking sector through a new partnership with Yapı Kredi, one of the country’s largest private banks. Under the agreement, the bank will leverage Ripple’s institutional-grade custody technology to strengthen its growing digital asset operations.

The partnership will see Ripple Custody support digital asset safekeeping for Yapı Kredi Kripto, the bank’s cryptocurrency trading platform. Deployed directly on the bank’s premises, the technology gives Yapı Kredi greater security and control over its customers’ digital asset holdings while providing the infrastructure needed to expand its crypto services.

The deal also puts Ripple in a market with considerable cryptocurrency adoption potential. Türkiye is already the largest retail crypto market in the Middle East and Africa and ranks among the world’s top 10. XRP is also one of the most widely held digital assets in the country, giving Ripple an opportunity to deepen its institutional presence in a market where the token already has an established following.

“As digital assets become an increasingly important part of the financial ecosystem, we’re focused on building the secure, reliable infrastructure needed to support this evolution,” Eylem Karaca, EVP, Core Banking, Lending, Treasury & Investment Technologies, Yapı Kredi Technology, posited. “Working with Ripple allows us to strengthen our digital asset custody capabilities and support the continued development of Yapı Kredi Kripto, while maintaining the security and trust our customers expect from Yapı Kredi.”

Meanwhile, Türkiye’s regulatory environment is evolving. The country’s Capital Markets Board (CMB) introduced a regulatory framework for crypto asset service providers in 2024, marking an important step toward bringing the industry under formal oversight. This regulatory progress, combined with growing institutional participation, could create further opportunities for Ripple’s custody business.

The discussion gained traction after crypto commentator Vincent Van Code shared an intriguing theory on X, suggesting Ripple could be several months into an ambitious initiative to shift payment flows from its acquired businesses to XRP and the XRP Ledger (XRPL).

According to Van Code, Ripple may already be eight months into an 18-month project to integrate its acquisitions into the XRP ecosystem. He estimated that the initiative could eventually bring approximately $16 trillion in annual payment volume onto the network over the next two to three years, potentially creating a significant new source of demand if the migration involves substantial XRP usage.

When pressed on how confident he was in his assessment, Van Code reiterated that his theory was based on professional experience and logical deductions rather than insider information. He pointed to his two decades of experience building enterprise strategies and systems, arguing that an integration project of this scale would reasonably take around 18 months to complete.

He further reasoned that Ripple’s acquisitions are about a year old, suggesting that the company could have launched the integration process roughly eight months ago. In his view, the acquisitions of GTreasury and Hidden Road make more sense when considered as part of a broader strategy to bring institutional payment flows into the XRP ecosystem.

Van Code further indicated that his confidence in Ripple’s alleged migration strategy should not be confused with certainty about XRP’s future price performance. While he believes Ripple intends to move substantial payment flows from its acquired businesses onto XRP and the XRPL, he acknowledged that neither he nor Ripple can determine exactly how much the token could rocket or when such a rally might happen.

Nevertheless, he argued that GTreasury’s corporate customers alone represent an enormous opportunity, with approximately $13 trillion in annual payment flows involving multiple currency pairs that require deep liquidity to facilitate cross-border transactions. Adding Hidden Road’s estimated $3 trillion in annual clearing volume brings the combined figure to roughly $16 trillion.

Based on this thesis, Van Code estimates that migrating just 30% of that payment volume onto XRP and the XRPL could push the token into the $15-$20 range by the end of 2027. He then outlined an even more ambitious scenario, suggesting that if the entire volume migrates and another $10 trillion is added by 2030, XRP could potentially reach $500-$600.

Hold on, I said I am confident that this is Ripples plan.. Whether the price pumps accordingly, how much and by when, I got no idea dude, no one does, not even Ripple.But my judgement tells me that the GTreasury customers alone payments to global economies has multiple currency…

XRP is currently trading at $0.9383, according to CoinGecko data. For the payments token to reach $600, it would need to surge by an astonishing 63,845%, representing roughly a 639-fold increase from its current price. Such an astronomical rally would require an unprecedented expansion in XRP’s market valuation, making Van Code’s long-term scenario an especially ambitious bet on Ripple’s ability to migrate substantial institutional payment flows onto the XRP Ledger.

For perspective, CoinGecko currently reports XRP’s circulating supply at approximately 63.5 billion tokens. At $600 per token, that would imply a market capitalization of a whopping $38.1 trillion, assuming supply remains unchanged.

In a follow-up X post, he described the $600 valuation scenario as the closest he would ever come to forecasting XRP’s price, emphasizing that it was merely an educated estimate based on the assumption that Ripple successfully executes its broader strategic plans.

#5071. Binance Rethinks VIP Eligibility as Investors Spread Capital Across Traditional and Crypto Markets

Home » Exchanges » Binance Rethinks VIP Eligibility as Investors Spread Capital Across Traditional and Crypto Markets

Binance expands VIP eligibility to include trading activity and asset holdings across external financial platforms.

Binance is adapting its VIP program to recognize financial activity across multiple markets, introducing a new initiative that allows investors to qualify for higher exchange status based on assets held and trading volumes generated on other platforms.

As cryptocurrency and traditional financial markets become increasingly interconnected, high-value investors are managing capital across a growing number of exchanges, investment products, and asset classes. Binance’s new VIP Status Match program aims to account for this shift by allowing individuals and institutions to demonstrate their financial activity beyond the exchange itself.

The initiative is part of a broader series of changes Binance has made to its VIP offering in 2026. In March, the exchange lowered BNB holding and Futures volume thresholds for VIP 1–3, introduced a Holder Program recognizing BNB and Alpha asset holdings across tiers up to VIP 9, and launched VIP Rising Star.

In July, Binance further reduced the wallet asset requirement for VIP 3 from $3 million to $1 million and began counting OTC Spot Volume at four times its value toward Spot Volume requirements.

The exchange also introduced a limited-time promotion running through the end of 2026, under which Stocks and bStocks trading volume counts at three times its value toward the 30-day VIP Spot Volume threshold. The initiative requires no registration and gives regular users and VIP 1–2 members a faster route to the next tier.

The latest addition, VIP Status Match, takes this approach further by allowing applicants to submit evidence of their 30-day trading volume or asset holdings on other digital asset exchanges or traditional financial platforms. Binance evaluates the information against its own VIP criteria to determine the appropriate tier.

Catherine Chen, Head of VIP & Institutional at Binance, said, “In 2024, we started recognizing trading activity from beyond crypto and we continue to refine our VIP Program to better reflect how our users engage across the platform. High-value users today trade and hold across multiple venues, so recognition should travel with them, not stay behind. Status Match does that, while keeping tier recognition tied to clear, measurable criteria.”

Both new and existing Binance users can apply. Applications are reviewed within three business days, and successful applicants receive an upgrade one tier above their qualifying level for 60 days, up to VIP 9. Upgraded trading fee rates take effect immediately upon approval, and participants are assigned a dedicated account manager.

Depending on their qualifying tier, users can also access benefits including VIP Earn, which offers up to 20% higher APR, Capital Connect for VIP 3 and above, customized API limits, sub-account management, and VIP events.

The program builds on Binance’s 2024 VIP Invitation Program but introduces broader eligibility. While the earlier initiative recognized trading activity beyond crypto, Status Match also accepts asset holdings as a qualifying metric and extends participation to existing Binance users.

The additional VIP tier is temporary. After 60 days, Binance will reassess participants against its standard requirements, including BNB balance, spot and derivatives trading volume, wallet assets, and 30-day average net borrowing. Users who meet the thresholds for their upgraded tier will retain it, while others will move to the level supported by their activity.

Through these changes, Binance is seeking to align VIP recognition with how investors allocate and manage capital across the wider financial ecosystem.

Bitcoin's 90-day correlation with gold has reached its highest level on record, according to Galaxy Research data. The measure peaked at 0.56 on Oct. 22 and broke the previous record of 0.50, which Galaxy dated to Nov. 6, 2020.

Alex Thorn, head of firmwide research at Galaxy Digital, posted about the record on X on Friday. "Bitcoin isn't digital gold? Bitcoin reaches highest correlation to gold of all time," he wrote.

Thorn shared two Galaxy Research charts together with the post. According to the charts, the 90-day correlation was at 0.54 on Nov. 23, and the 30-day correlation stood at 0.59 on the same day.

In the first half of 2026, the 90-day correlation stayed near 0.1. It started to rise in July and climbed above 0.50 by early October, according to Galaxy's data. Between 2020 and 2025, the average reading was 0.11.

On Jan. 20, Galaxy CEO Mike Novogratz wrote on X that "the gold price is telling us we are losing reserve currency status at an accelerating rate." "$BTC is disappointing as it is still being met with selling," he added.

Thorn wrote about Bitcoin and gold on X in February. "Bitcoin's failure to trade like gold as part of 'the debasement trade' since Sep. '25 damaged its narrative with new entrants," he wrote. "When bitcoiners said 'digital gold,' they were describing its fundamental properties, not that it's high beta to gold today," he added.

On Wednesday, Galaxy published a report that withdrew its Oct. 26 call on the Bitcoin bear market. "We withdraw our call that the bear market ended in June," the report said. Thorn shared it on X with the comment, "As it turns out, the Bitcoin bear market is definitely not over."

According to the report, Bitcoin closed the week ended Nov. 22 at $61,104 after seven straight weekly losses. Thorn wrote in the report that the level to watch was $58,525, Bitcoin's closing low from June 30. According to Thorn, a daily close below that level would mark "the start of a move to a materially lower low."

"The clock says this bear is overdue to end; the depth says it has further to fall," the report said. On Nov. 22, the bear market was 412 days old, and earlier ones lasted 163 to 406 days from high to low, according to Galaxy.

Bitcoin was down 53% from its October 2025 record at that point. In past bear markets, it lost 77% to 93%. If the June low breaks, Galaxy sees possible new lows at about $48,500 and $28,200.

Galaxy tracks 13 bottom signals, and two of them have been met so far. According to the report, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETPs held about 1.24 million BTC, down 71,339 BTC since Oct. 4.

On Nov. 17, SkyBridge Capital founder Anthony Scaramucci asked Novogratz at the Digital Assets Forum in New York whether Bitcoin could return to $90,000 by the end of 2026. "Unlikely now," Novogratz said. "Less likely than it was. You need something to happen," he added.

#5068. Crypto market maker Auros is reportedly winding down

Auros, a Hong Kong crypto market maker that says it handled roughly 4% of global exchange volume as of July 2024, is winding down, according to a report citing two people with knowledge of the situation.

Crypto market maker Auros is winding down its operations, CoinDesk reported on November 26, 2026, citing two people with knowledge of the situation. Auros has not publicly confirmed the wind-down.

Nothing is public yet about why the firm is closing, how long the wind-down will take, or whether it will run through a formal restructuring or insolvency process.

The size of what would be leaving the market is large by Auros’s own account. Its website lists more than $1.3 trillion of 2025 trading volume so far and a record day of $18.2 billion; neither figure is audited. Co-founder Ben Roth, the firm’s chief investment officer, put its share of global exchange trading at about 4% in July 2024, and Auros says it quotes more than 3,000 instruments on over 50 venues.

Auros started trading in 2019 and became one of the bigger liquidity providers in crypto. FTX’s failure in November 2022 froze part of its money on the exchange and pushed it into provisional liquidation under a British Virgin Islands court. Fresh capital arrived in March 2023: $17 million, with Vivienne Court as lead investor and Bit Digital also taking part, and the firm left provisional liquidation the same month.

A venture arm followed in July 2024, with a plan to put over $50 million of the firm’s own money into young crypto startups within two years; Pyth, the price-data network, and Berachain were among its bets.

Two months ago, on September 29, 2026, Auros rolled out Aurora, an institutional trading portal that opens both centralized exchange and DeFi liquidity to professional clients. It also names Sei, Horizen, Nibiru Chain and Aethir as ecosystems where it supports trading.

#5066. Solana Playground Adds AI Agent for Smart Contract Developers

Home » Altcoins » Solana (SOL) » Solana Playground Adds AI Agent for Smart Contract Developers

The updated browser workspace adds an in-editor assistant as Solana expands its wider AI developer push.

Solana has rolled out a built-in AI coding agent inside Solana Playground, its browser-based development environment, aiming to help programmers learn, build, and deploy smart contracts without setting up local toolchains.

For traders and investors, it offers useful context on developer onboarding, Solana’s AI infrastructure push, and early-stage protocol risk.

In a post on X, Solana introduced the updated Solana Playground as a place to “learn, build and deploy Solana programs right in your browser,” noting that the integrated agent explains existing code and edits it alongside the developer rather than writing full programs on its own.

Introducing Solana Playground – where you learn, build and deploy Solana programs right in your browser. An AI agent explains the code and edits it with you. Start here: https://t.co/nM0ySqDkfO pic.twitter.com/SFKYYTx04n

Builders can start projects using either Anchor, a framework that streamlines Solana program development, or native Solana programming, which offers lower-level control without framework abstractions.

According to product walk-throughs, the workspace includes three guided learning paths. These include an introductory Anchor tutorial called Hello Anchor and an intermediate build named Lumberjack. It also offers 10 sample Solana programs.

Browser-based Solana development predates the AI integration: the open-source Solana Playground (SolPg) has long let developers compile Rust programs, manage development wallets, and deploy contracts without a local CLI setup.

The latest release adds an in-editor assistant to explain unfamiliar code and apply edits within the same session.

The Playground update fits into a wider push around AI and automated agents on Solana.

Solana’s developer portal now provides guidance for AI coding agents, while solana.ai focuses on autonomous trading, wallet management, and stablecoin payments.

The Solana Foundation has also introduced an open-source Confidential Compute toolkit with Nito for AI workloads involving sensitive data.

Figures shared by the Solana Foundation at Breakpoint 2026 indicated more than 120 teams are building AI products on Solana, with access to the Builder Program for grants, technical resources, hiring support, marketing help, and infrastructure credits.

Developer-focused releases rarely drive sustained moves in SOL or ecosystem tokens on their own. Liquidity, macro conditions, and net capital flows carry far more weight in the near term.

However, lowering the barrier to write and iterate on code can speed up experimentation—and increase the volume of new or lightly tested contracts. Developer activity remains a key indicator of long-term ecosystem growth.

#5065. Bitcoin Whales Buy Over 121,000 BTC Despite 29.5% Price Crash

Bitcoin whales have defied the negative trend seen in the Q4s of the past nine years as they have accumulated billions of dollars' worth of Bitcoin since Q4 2026 began.

Even though Bitcoin has faced severe price corrections during the period, with its price retesting levels not seen this year, Bitcoin whales have continued to buy the asset.

Onchain data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant shows that Bitcoin wallet addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC have increased their holdings by 121,117 BTC in Q4 2026.

This defies the trend seen in the last nine Q4s, as Bitcoin whales have historically reduced their holdings during Q4 of each of the last nine years.

The source shared historic data from 2017, revealing that the Bitcoin whales recorded balance declines in seven of the last nine Q4 periods, with only 2019 and 2020 recording increases.

This means that the increase seen this month marks a major reversal of that historical trend, especially as Bitcoin has suffered even bigger price losses this Q4, dropping by about 29.5% over the same 52-day period.

Following the increase in Bitcoin whale accumulation seen in this quarter, further data shows that the whales now hold about 2.947 million BTC as of November 21, 2026.

Despite the increase in the holdings of Bitcoin whales this Q4, data also showed that these large holders have seen their unrealized profits drop significantly.

As such, unrealized profits among addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC have fallen to about $23.8 billion. Notably, this represents a massive decrease from the $124.7 billion recorded on September 30 and the record $294.4 billion in gains achieved on August 14, 2025.

#5063. Monero’s Delisting Nightmare Continues: XMR Price Plunges 15%

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Data from BitInfoCharts shows that Monero fell from $525.36 to $446.54 during Thursday’s trading session. For longtime XMR investors, the sell-off is an uncomfortable reminder of what happened when Binance announced its Monero delisting in February 2024.

This time, however, the list of major exchanges available to Monero traders is considerably shorter.

In a November 26 announcement, KuCoin confirmed that it will remove all four Monero spot trading pairs against USDT, USDC, ETH and BTC on November 30 at 08:00 UTC.

The exchange has already suspended XMR deposits and does not intend to reopen them. Withdrawals are scheduled to remain available until December 31 at 08:00 UTC, although KuCoin reserves the right to close them earlier if problems affecting the network arise.

Monero’s removal extends beyond spot trading. KuCoin will discontinue XMR flexible savings on November 27, followed by its conversion and automated trading services on November 30.

There is another detail in the announcement that deserves particular attention. KuCoin will stop accepting XMR as collateral for its VIP loan products. Customers who have borrowed against their Monero holdings may need to provide alternative collateral to avoid liquidation.

For holders planning to leave their coins on the exchange until the withdrawal deadline, KuCoin also warned that remaining balances could be converted into stablecoins, although “such conversion is not guaranteed.”

The exchange cited its platform policies but did not identify a specific regulatory requirement behind the decision.

KuCoin is not the first exchange to abandon Monero this month, but its departure could prove particularly significant given the amount of XMR trading it handles.

A November 26 snapshot from CoinGecko identified KuCoin as Monero’s most active exchange, with its XMR/USDT pair recording approximately $62.6 million in trading volume over a 24-hour period.

Earlier this month, MEXC discontinued spot trading for Monero on November 17. Binance removed the cryptocurrency in February 2024, while Kraken halted XMR trading for European Economic Area customers in October of the same year, explicitly citing regulatory changes.

Trading volume does not simply disappear when an exchange delists an asset. Some of it will move elsewhere, and investors who intend to keep their holdings can withdraw them to private wallets.

The bigger question is how efficiently the remaining exchanges can absorb that activity. If fewer venues are competing for the same orders, particularly during periods of market stress, large trades could become more expensive to execute and price swings more pronounced.

For Monero, that is increasingly a market structure problem rather than a question of whether its underlying technology works.

There is a case against assuming that Thursday’s sell-off marks the beginning of a prolonged decline.

Monero has survived previous exchange removals and even managed to establish new price highs in 2026 despite mounting restrictions. As NewsBTC previously reported, XMR traded above $700 earlier this year, long after Binance stopped supporting its spot markets.

But a functioning network does not guarantee a liquid market. Investors still need practical ways to enter and exit their positions without incurring excessive trading costs.

November 30 will therefore be an important test for Monero. Rather than focusing solely on whether XMR recovers the $500 level, traders should watch where KuCoin’s trading volume migrates and whether the remaining exchanges can absorb larger orders without substantial slippage.

That will offer a better indication of whether Thursday’s decline was a temporary reaction to another delisting or a warning of a deeper liquidity problem.

#5062. Bitcoin Developer Warns Google Play Policy Could Lead to Home Invasions

On Nov. 27, Bitcoin developer Peter Todd warned that Google's plan to publicly display developers' addresses on the Play Store could lead to home invasions targeting developers of Bitcoin apps.

For independent developers working from home, the address displayed on Google Play could also be their residential address.

"There will be home invasions to compromise developers," Todd wrote on X.

He specifically highlighted the risks to developers of Bitcoin and other security-related apps, urging Google employees responsible for implementing the change to refuse to do so.

Starting March 1, 2027, Google Play will display the phone number and address of developers who use individual accounts to publish apps and identify themselves as traders.

Google explained that the requirement is related to its obligations as an online marketplace in the European Economic Area (EEA) and the UK.

The address and contact information will be visible to Play Store users worldwide.

The question is what address a developer might have to disclose, even for a relatively small app.

Dodemaide explained that Google support had informed him that he couldn't use a post office box because the address had to match his verified residential address.

He said he was considering removing his app from 31 countries to protect his home address.

Dodemaide also asked whether Google would allow individual developers to use a verified business mailing address instead.

Google lists several types of developers who may need to consider whether they qualify as traders, including those who sell apps, offer in-app purchases or earn advertising revenue.

For example, someone publishing an app purely as a hobby could declare themselves a non-trader.

Developers who don't distribute their apps in the EEA or UK are also considered non-traders under the policy.

Existing account holders have until Feb. 1, 2027, to submit their trader declarations, one month before the contact information becomes publicly visible.

Developers creating new accounts will need to make their declarations during account registration.

Google warns that failing to comply could prevent developers from updating their apps or result in their apps being removed from the Play Store globally.

#5061. Bitcoin wallet privacy at risk? Researcher claims $0.35 attack could expose users’ IP addresses

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

This vulnerability was identified by Bitcoin Core contributor Abubakar Sadiq Ismail in a post on the Delving Bitcoin developer forum. As it stands, although Bitcoin transactions are publicly recorded, wallet addresses are pseudonymous, meaning users can view transaction details without knowing who controls them.

Similarly, Bitcoin’s P2P network makes it difficult to link a wallet to a specific computer.

Well, according to researcher Sadeeq, the answer may be yes because of a weakness in how Bitcoin Core handles transaction rebroadcasting.

To understand the vulnerability, it is important to know how Bitcoin Core works. So, many users operate their own nodes, which maintain blockchain copies, validate transactions, and communicate with other nodes. These nodes can also run wallets that track Bitcoin addresses.

Each node has an IP address that can reveal its internet provider and approximate location. However, a wallet address does not normally expose the IP address of the computer tracking it. Hence, the vulnerability arises because Bitcoin Core may rebroadcast transactions that remain unconfirmed for approximately 12 to 36 hours.

According to the researcher, an attacker can exploit this by sending a small, low-fee payment to a targeted address. For this, the payment must meet Bitcoin’s minimum dust threshold while carrying a low enough fee to remain unconfirmed. Going forward, the attacker could then wait for the wallet to rebroadcast the planted transaction while monitoring different Bitcoin nodes.

When one node announces the transaction again, the attacker can identify it as the node whose wallet tracks the targeted address. This, in turn, would theoretically link the Bitcoin address to the node’s IP address, exposing information about its internet connection.

On the question of simulation involving five target wallets across six trials, Sadeeq successfully identified the correct wallet-tracking node in all 30 attempts. However, this does not necessarily reveal who owns the Bitcoin.

Hence, as a potential workaround, users can disable automatic wallet broadcasting through the -walletbroadcast=0 setting. However, this might lead to another problem, and that is that it stops automatic broadcasting of their own transactions. Therefore, proposed Bitcoin Core changes aim to address the issue, but they remain unreleased.

Here, it’s worth noting that these revelations coincided with the percentage of Bitcoin wallets currently at a loss entering a capitulation zone — historically associated with major market reversals. This could also mean that while retail investors panic, larger investors may be preparing to accumulate.

#5060. Midnight Savings Launch Puts NIGHT Ahead Of ADA

Home » Trendsetter News » Midnight Savings Launch Puts NIGHT Ahead Of ADA

Monument Bank’s Midnight rollout links banking activity more directly to NIGHT than ADA, but its £250M bid reflects initial capacity.

The £250 million figure attached to Monument Bank’s Midnight rollout is an initial capacity limit, not confirmed customer deposits, according to a video from crypto commentator FireHustle.

That distinction sits at the heart of the host’s analysis: a bank adopting technology built by Cardano’s developers does not necessarily translate into immediate demand for ADA.

Its potential significance lies less in the headline amount than in which token benefits from the activity.

According to Fire Hustle, Monument’s offering pays existing customers a fixed 5.2% for one year. Account details remain private, and customers cannot sell or transfer the blockchain records, even to another Monument customer.

Cardano’s Founder Charles Hoskinson celebrated the rollout with the phrase “250 million pounds on-chain.” But the host says Monument has not disclosed actual deposits, despite tokens representing the full initial allocation already having been created.

The YouTube video also cites Midnight Foundation president Fahmi Syed saying seven other banks are considering similar products: six in Canada and one in Japan.

Canada merits attention because Calgary-based digital-asset custodian Balance handles Monument’s tokens, according to the video. The host explicitly cautions against assuming the unnamed institutions are Canada’s six largest banks.

Midnight’s token structure is the investment question. The video says holding NIGHT generates DUST, the resource used to pay network transaction fees. Banks or service providers can therefore cover customers’ activity without requiring savers to handle tokens themselves.

“Somebody still has to hold the Night that makes the Dust,” she says. That creates a more direct connection between Midnight usage and NIGHT than between that usage and ADA, although additional activity does not guarantee token-price gains.

The ADA connection is more distant. Cardano stake-pool operators are expected to help secure Midnight in early 2027, with potential rewards extending to their ADA delegators. Those rewards are prospective, not existing income.

Fire Hustle reports ADA trading more than 90% below its peak at recording. However, the more useful indicators are actual Monument deposits, transaction volumes and confirmed bank launches.

The XRP Ledger's native lending protocol entered a 14-day activation countdown on Friday after its amendments gained 29 of 35 validator votes, according to XRPScan. If support holds, the ledger will get native lending and borrowing as early as Dec. 11, for the first time since its launch in 2012.

Hussein Zangana, director of community at the XRP Ledger Foundation, cast the 29th vote with his validator and announced it in an X post on Friday. "I vote now for the Lending Protocol on the XRP Ledger and it's now in activation with 29 Yes votes," Zangana wrote.

𝗜 𝘃𝗼𝘁𝗲 𝗻𝗼𝘄 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗲 Lending Protocol 𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 XRP Ledger and it's now in activation with 29 Yes votes. 𝗩𝗲𝘁 𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗲𝘀📝: Lending and borrowing unlock capital and liquidity on the XRP Ledger, provide yield and make XRP and XRPL assets usable as collateral. I appreciate the efforts exercised by the community to give this amendment a good screening! For validators this is important assistance and help in making educated decisions. Let's dive into why i voted Yes for Lending on XRP🧵.

According to XRPScan, LendingProtocol and its update LendingProtocolV1_1 both reached 29 votes on Friday. The earliest activation date for LendingProtocolV1_1 is Dec. 11, and its support has to stay above 80% until then. SingleAssetVault, the third amendment in the package, has 30 votes and can activate as early as Dec. 9.

"Lending and borrowing unlock capital and liquidity on the XRP Ledger, provide yield and make XRP and XRPL assets usable as collateral," Zangana added in the same post.

Ripple engineer Vito Tumas first proposed the protocol in April 2024. According to the XLS-65 standard, each Single Asset Vault holds only one asset, such as XRP or RLUSD, and depositors get vault shares in the form of Multi-Purpose Tokens.

Under XLS-66, a loan broker uses that capital to issue loans with a fixed term and a fixed rate. The broker checks borrowers off-chain and can post its own first-loss capital to cover defaults. Interest payments go back into the vault, and the protocol has no on-chain liquidations.

"Represent value. Move value. Trade value. Now: finance value," Jazzi Cooper, head of product at RippleX, wrote on X about the vote. According to Cooper, the team made "deliberate design decisions: protocol native, built-in compliance, and off-chain underwriting."

J. Ayo Akinyele, head of engineering at RippleX, wrote that the vaults and the protocol went through "multiple independent audits, a public Attackathon, formal verification, AI-assisted reviews, community testing, and validator review." Ripple and Common Prefix did the formal verification in the Lean 4 theorem prover. "Traditional testing isn't enough when you're building DeFi directly into Layer-1," Tumas wrote.

Clearpool said that it would bring "real-world, institutional-ready lending infrastructure, built natively on XRPL." The platform plans a credit fund on the ledger with Ripple and Cicada Partners, and it has already tested a full loan cycle on Devnet. "We want to make real loans to real businesses," Tom Lombardi of Cicada Partners said.

Evernorth CEO Ashish Birla said that his company "is exploring how XLS-66 could support yield generation as part of our broader treasury strategy."

According to XRPScan, SingleAssetVault can go live on Dec. 9, and the two lending amendments can follow on Dec. 11 if their support holds.

#5058. Michael Saylor’s Net Worth Plunges $6 Billion: The Cost of His Bitcoin Bet

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Michael Saylor’s net worth has fallen by approximately $6 billion since the cryptocurrency market peaked in October 2025. The Strategy co-founder, whose fortune was estimated at $9.3 billion at the time, is now worth around $3.3 billion, according to Forbes.

The decline has wiped out nearly two-thirds of Saylor’s estimated wealth. Yet the billionaire’s company continues to accumulate Bitcoin despite mounting paper losses, showing little willingness to reconsider its investment strategy.

For Saylor, the downturn presents a problem that extends well beyond the price of Bitcoin. Much of his fortune depends on a company that must convince investors to keep financing its accumulation strategy.

Saylor was already among the cryptocurrency industry’s biggest financial casualties in February, when Forbes estimated that his wealth had fallen by $4.7 billion from its October 2025 level.

His fortune briefly stabilized in the following months, reaching an estimated $4.7 billion in June, before suffering another setback.

The latest estimate puts Saylor’s wealth approximately 64.5% below its October 2025 level.

Bitcoin’s return to the $60,000 level has added pressure, but the cryptocurrency alone does not explain the scale of the decline. Saylor’s exposure through Strategy makes his financial position considerably more complicated than that of an ordinary Bitcoin investor.

The $6 billion represents a reduction in estimated wealth, not a confirmed cash loss or the proceeds of any disclosed asset sales.

In October 2020, Saylor disclosed that he personally owned 17,732 BTC, acquired for approximately $175 million.

At the Bitcoin price of $60,325 reported by Strategy on November 26, those holdings would be worth approximately $1.07 billion, assuming he still owns the entire disclosed amount.

That would leave his original personal investment with an unrealized gain of roughly $895 million.

His current personal Bitcoin balance has not been independently confirmed, but the calculation illustrates an important distinction. Saylor can lose billions in estimated wealth while remaining substantially profitable on his original Bitcoin purchases.

The situation at Strategy is quite different.

While Saylor began buying Bitcoin at considerably lower prices, his company has spent much of the past several years increasing its exposure at higher valuations.

According to its November 23 SEC filing, Strategy acquired another 457 BTC for $29.6 million, bringing its total holdings to 851,305 BTC.

The company has spent approximately $64.23 billion accumulating Bitcoin at an average purchase price of $75,446.

Its official Bitcoin dashboard valued those reserves at approximately $51.35 billion on November 26.

That leaves a gap of nearly $12.9 billion between the company’s cumulative acquisition cost and the market value of its Bitcoin holdings.

These figures do not represent realized trading losses, nor do they capture the full financial performance of the company.

Nevertheless, the numbers reveal how dramatically the economics of accumulating Bitcoin have changed during the downturn.

For years, investors were willing to pay a premium for Strategy shares. The attraction was not simply the Bitcoin it owned, but the prospect that management could raise additional capital and increase shareholders’ exposure to the cryptocurrency.

That premium is no longer something the company can take for granted.

Strategy’s dashboard showed an mNAV ratio of 0.94 at the November 25 stock market close, using its own net Bitcoin value per share methodology.

The company’s latest investor briefing acknowledges the implications:

A widening discount can cause MSTR to underperform BTC even when bitcoin rises.

This is where Saylor’s investment model faces a more difficult test.

When investors are willing to pay a premium for Strategy shares, raising capital to acquire more Bitcoin can improve the economics of the business. When that premium disappears, issuing additional shares becomes a more complicated proposition.

Strategy’s own sensitivity analysis shows that a Bitcoin price of $40,000 would reduce its estimated net reserve value per share to $45.37, compared with $163.17 at a Bitcoin price of $100,000. The figures illustrate how sensitive the company’s underlying reserve valuation is to Bitcoin price movements.

Strategy’s third-quarter financial results offer a clearer picture of why its cash reserves and financing obligations now matter almost as much as the price of Bitcoin.

Buying more Bitcoin is only one part of the equation. The cost of financing those purchases matters just as much.

There is a credible case for recovery. Strategy still owns more than 850,000 Bitcoin, giving it considerable exposure to any sustained cryptocurrency market rebound.

The company also reported approximately $4.82 billion in combined cash and dollar reserves in its latest investor briefing, providing a buffer against its financing obligations.

But a recovery in Bitcoin would not necessarily produce an equivalent recovery in Saylor’s wealth. Strategy’s share price also depends on its debt, preferred-stock obligations, access to capital and the valuation investors are willing to assign to its business model.

The next test for Saylor is not whether he can buy another thousand Bitcoin. It is whether he can continue financing those purchases on terms that benefit existing shareholders.

His personal fortune has already demonstrated how expensive that distinction can become.

The project says its next phase will focus on building the listings system, advisors, and token-payment functionality in parallel.

CoinMarketCap recorded $CON’s launch-period low at approximately $0.009144 on November 6. The token subsequently reached an all-time high of approximately $0.08434 on November 24. In the November 26 snapshot, it was trading at approximately $0.06582, representing an increase of about 619.9% from its recorded low.

The movement has not been a continuous upward trend. After its initial market debut, $CON experienced price fluctuations before reaching a new all-time high later in November. Such volatility can occur during the early trading period of a newly launched cryptocurrency, as buyers and sellers establish a market price. The token’s current distance from its latest high is therefore worth monitoring alongside its longer-term performance.

The November 26 CoinMarketCap snapshot showed a market capitalisation of approximately $3.01 million and 24-hour trading volume of about $155,650. It also reported approximately 2,180 holders. These figures provide a more recent view of market participation than the November 12 snapshot.

The token’s performance occurred during a difficult month for the broader crypto market. ConConAI says $CON’s movement has been driven by its own fundamentals, including a live product, transparent token information, and continued development. That explanation reflects the project’s position; price movement alone cannot establish what caused buying interest, and the broader market can still affect $CON.

Several developments give $CON a potentially constructive outlook as it moves beyond its initial listing period.

First, the token has established market visibility through its CoinMarketCap and CoinGecko listings, its reported first-day top-gainer position, and its early trading performance. Continued visibility could bring additional market participants to the project, although listings and past gains do not guarantee future demand.

Second, ConConAI has reported that 40.15 million tokens have been burned from the original 100 million supply, leaving an effective supply of 59.85 million $CON. The first two burns removed 20 million tokens each, followed by a monthly burn of 150,000 $CON on November 19. The project says further 150,000-token burns are scheduled monthly, with the next one planned for December 15. Future burns remain scheduled events until completed and verified on-chain.

Third, the token has a planned utility within ConConAI’s commercial network. If the platform attracts consumers and businesses, the intended use of $CON for partner listings, placements, and performance-based fees could create a more substantial demand story than trading interest alone. The development tracker currently places the first partner payments in $CON in February 2027.

From the November 26 reference price of approximately $0.06582, a return to the November 24 high of $0.08434 would represent potential appreciation of around 28.1%. The combination of early market strength, reduced token supply, and an evolving utility model gives market participants several reasons to consider buying $CON.

ConConAI’s broader proposition is built around bringing back the personal purchase advisor, powered by artificial intelligence. Instead of navigating endless search results and comparing countless products, users describe what they need. A specialist AI advisor asks relevant questions, interprets the requirements, and returns one recommendation with the reason behind it.

The consumer remains in control. The AI does not make purchases on the user’s behalf, and the final decision always belongs to the user.

Seven specialist advisors are live, covering categories that include investment guidance, travel, cars, film, health information, music, and real estate. The project’s aim is to make AI useful in everyday purchasing decisions by helping people move from describing a need to identifying a relevant option.

Businesses can also submit products and services to the network. ConConAI’s stated model is that payment does not buy recommendation rank: a listing is intended to appear only when it honestly matches what the user asked for, with fit taking priority. This approach is designed to connect consumers with suitable offers while giving participating businesses another way to reach potential customers.

ConConAI says development capacity has been scaled up, with the listings system, advisors, and $CON payments now being built in parallel. Its public development tracker is updated as progress happens and identifies current work on partner listings, advisor improvements, and payment functionality. The project plans to begin its first partner payments in $CON in February 2027.

The exchange roadmap has also changed. ConConAI now says four Tier 2 centralized exchange listings are planned for December 2026, one after another. The project says each listing will be announced once confirmed. These are plans, not confirmed listing agreements, and should not be treated as guaranteed dates or outcomes.

The MEXC listing is currently on hold because of the exchange’s regulatory situation. ConConAI says it will review the situation from December 10, after which the MEXC listing may proceed or be replaced by another Tier 1 exchange. Until an exchange makes its own announcement or an agreement is confirmed, the plans remain subject to change.

The $CON presale sold out on November 4, and the token has traded on Uniswap v4’s official CON/ETH pool since November 6, 2026. Its liquidity position is reported to be locked with UNCX until November 6, 2028. The project says pool fees currently help cover development and marketing costs, with partner payments expected to contribute once the listings platform opens.

ConConAI reports that the live $CON contract audit has been completed. It also cites a TokenSniffer score of 100/100, contract verification on Etherscan, and listings on CoinMarketCap, CoinGecko, DEXTools, and DexScreener. These are useful verification and discovery signals, but they do not eliminate market, smart-contract or third-party platform risks.

The project’s transparency page provides live wallet balances and burn records. Its published allocation includes 30 million $CON for the community, 15 million for liquidity, 10 million for centralized-exchange liquidity, and approximately 5 million for project purposes. The project says its allocation wallets use Safe multisig arrangements. The official contract address is 0x7ad1A8Fc42Ac150B04dED5825D21a0C90b6d28D8.

$CON’s early market performance has given ConConAI a strong starting point following its Uniswap debut. Its ability to maintain interest will increasingly depend on trading participation, liquidity, product delivery, and the development of real commercial activity around its AI advisors.

If the project converts its existing development progress into wider consumer adoption and partner participation, the token’s intended utility could become an increasingly important part of its market proposition. Combined with the reported supply reduction and community-led roadmap, these factors provide a positive basis for watching $CON’s next phase, while recognising the volatility and risks associated with newly launched crypto assets.

ConConAI is developing a network of AI-powered personal purchase advisors and commercial partner listings. Its $CON token is intended to support partner activity across the ecosystem, including listings, placements, and performance-based fees.

#5056. Analyst: Ripple’s Growth Doesn’t Guarantee $10 XRP

Home » Trendsetter News » Analyst: Ripple’s Growth Doesn’t Guarantee $10 XRP

Ripple’s expansion alone won’t send XRP to $10, a popular wealth coach states.

A $10 XRP would imply a circulating market value of roughly $630 billion, not simply another rally on Ripple announcements.

That is the central argument from Dr. Kamilah Stevenson, a wealth coach whose latest YouTube video episode examines why the company’s institutional expansion has not translated into the token price many holders expected.

Using approximately 63 billion XRP in circulation, Stevenson argues that reaching that XRP valuation requires more than partnerships and regulatory milestones. It requires sustained demand to own the token, rather than merely move money through it.

Stevenson separates Ripple’s corporate performance, adoption of its products, demand for XRP and the token’s market price. Those categories overlap, but they are not interchangeable: a customer using Ripple’s custody services or stablecoin does not necessarily need XRP.

Even payments routed through XRP may generate limited lasting demand. In the process she describes, a payment provider buys the token, transfers it and sells it into the destination currency within seconds, allowing the same inventory to support repeated transactions.

“Big payment numbers alone don’t automatically push the price up,” Dr. Stevenson says. The more consequential question is how much XRP participants need to keep available between transactions.

Market makers may hold inventory to support larger payment flows, creating a potential link between usage and ownership. Still, the video does not quantify how much additional inventory those flows would require.

Dr. Kamilah Stevenson cites roughly 1.19 billion XRP held by ETFs and about 473 million held by Evernorth, a company established to accumulate XRP. Those are figures presented in the video, rather than independently verified current totals.

Her distinction is useful: XRP-backed fund holdings represent direct token ownership, while the national trust bank approval she attributes to Ripple does not itself require institutions to purchase XRP.

Supply remains part of the calculation. Stevenson puts Ripple’s escrow holdings at around 31 billion XRP, with up to one billion released monthly and unused amounts returned to escrow. An unlock is therefore not equivalent to an immediate market sale.

The sharper test is whether an announcement creates incremental buying, how long those tokens stay held and whether new supply offsets that demand. Dr. Stevenson remains bullish, but the adoption figures she discusses do not establish when XRP reaches $10.
